To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with concordantly low molecular responses at 3 and 6 months have a significantly better prognosis than individuals with discordant responses.

1) BCR-ABL transcript levels at diagnosis and after 3 and 6 months of therapy are associated with clinical outcomes in CML patients, 2) the 6-month transcript level has a superior prognostication value compared to the transcript level measured after 3 months of treatment in CML patients with discordant molecular responses, and 3) patients with BCR-Abl transcript level >10% after 6 month of therapy have poor prognosis.

1) a 6-month BMR <1% is associated with superior clinical responses in chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), 2) a 3-month BMR >10% is associated with inferior clinical responses in CML, and 3) patients with discordant BCR-ABI levels at 3 and 6 months have an intermediate clinical response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of multiple early BCR-ABL levels as predictors of clinical outcomes in CML patients treated with imatinib.
the clinical implications of discordant early BCR-ABL/ABLIS transcripts in patients with CML treated with standard-dosed imatinib.
the clinical implications of discordant early molecular responses in CML patients treated with standard-dosage imatinib.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 6-month molecular response is more important in predicting the long-term prognosis than the 3-month response in patients with discordance between the two time points.
the 6-month level is the best predictor of long-term outcome, but the 3-month level should be considered in patients with discordantly low BCR-ABL at 3 months.
a reduction to <10% at month 3 and <1% at month 6 is associated with superior outcomes in chronic myleoid leukaemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with BCR/ABL1 levels below 10% after 12 weeks of treatment are at a significantly higher risk of treatment failure and relapse than patients with BCR/Abl levels above 10%.
the 6-month transcript level is the best prognostic marker in patients with discordance at both 3- and/or 6-month time point.
a 3-month BCR-AML1/ABL1 transcript value of >10% and <1% at the 6-month time point are associated with significantly superior outcomes in patients with CML treated with standard-doses of imatinib.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients who achieve BCR-ABL 1/ABL1 IS values below 1% at the 6-month time point are more likely to achieve deep molecular response, and thus should be considered for treatment intensification.
the 6-month molecular measurement is the best indicator of treatment response and should be used as a benchmark to assess treatment outcomes.
patients with discordant molecular responses at 3 and 6 months should not be grouped together, as they have significantly different clinical outcomes.
